cohort: Pregnant women or women immediately postpartum identified with a fibrinogen level below 2 g/L in any UK hospital with a consultant-led maternity unit.
finding: Low fibrinogen concentration (<2 g/L) was frequently caused by postpartum hemorrhage related to placental abruption, atony, or trauma, with other severe obstetric events also contributing, and was associated with extremely high maternal and perinatal mortality.
